1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. Rule.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Rule is made returnable forthwith with the consent of the parties and is taken up for final disposal.
Learned APP waives notice on behalf of the respondent No.1 - State.
Mr. Patil, waives 30-wpst.494.2023.doc notice on behalf of the respondent No.2 (original complainant).

3. By this petition, preferred under Article 226 of the Constitution of India and under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code, the petitioners seek quashing of the FIR bearing C.R. No. I-211 of 2015 registered with the Kharghar Police Station, Raigad,

sentences.text:
Quashing is sought on the premise, that the parties have amicably settled their dispute.
4.
Perused the papers.
The petitioner No.1 is the husband of the respondent No.2 and the petitioner Nos.2 and 3, mother-in-law and father-in-law respectively of the respondent No.2.
It appears that the respondent No.2 and the petitioner No.1 got married on 9 th December 2010.

As according to the respondent No.2, she was ill- treated and harassed by the petitioners, she lodged the aforesaid FIR, as against the petitioners,
alleging the aforesaid offences.

It appears that the respondent No.2 also filed a Domestic Violence complaint in 30-wpst.494.2023.doc the Court of the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class at Panvel being Criminal M.A. No.752 of 2017.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class at Panvel
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It appears that in the present C.R., the police after investigation have filed a charge-sheet and the case is presently pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class at Panvel being R.C.C. No.511 of 2017.
5.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class at Panvel
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the interregnum, during the pendency of the aforesaid proceeding, the parties amicably settled their dispute and decided to put a quietus to the same.
6. Learned Counsel for the respondent No.2 has tendered an affidavit of the respondent No.2 dated 17 th January 2023, duly notarised before the Notary.
To the said affidavit is annexed a self attested photocopy of the aadhar card of the respondent No. 2.

Consent terms entered into between the parties and tendered before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class at Panvel in the Domestic Violence proceeding have also been annexed to the said affidavit.

In 30-wpst.494.2023.doc the said affidavit, the respondent No.2 had given her no objection to the quashing of the aforesaid C.R/proceeding, in view of the amicable settlement between the parties and the consent terms entered into between her and the petitioner No.1.
A perusal of the consent terms shows that there are several terms and conditions stipulated therein.
It also appears that the petitioner No.1 is to pay the respondent No.2 a sum of Rs.16,50,000/- as and by way of full and final settlement in tranches.
The said tranches have been spelt out in paragraph 4 of the consent terms.
It is not in dispute that the petitioner No.1 has deposited the entire amout of Rs.16,50,000/- in the Court of the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class at Panvel i.e. the D.V. Court.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class at Panvel
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Respondent No. 2 is present in Court.
On being questioned, she re- iterates what is stated by her in her affidavit.
She does not dispute the fact that the petitioner No.1 has deposited Rs.16,50,000/- in the domestic violence proceeding.

Learned Counsel for the respondent No.2 has identified the respondent No.2 and the learned APP has also verified the original aadhar card of the respondent No.2.
30-wpst.494.2023.doc 7.

Considering the nature of dispute, the relationship between the parties, the amicable settlement between them, the affidavit of the respondent No.2 and having regard to the judicial pronouncements of the Apex Court in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr.1 and Narinder Singh &
Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. 2, there is no impediment in allowing the petition.
